Positioned pressure necessary for continuous ultrafiltration; JG cells in
afferent media release renin. Arise from efferent arterioles of cortical nephrons (~85%); form extensive Starling forces massively favor rapid tubular reabsorption of water,
sodium, and nutrients back into systemic venous circulation. meshwork around PCT & DCT in cortical labyrinth. Low hydrostatic pressure (~13 mmHg), high oncotic pressure (~32 mmHg).

Vasa Recta Spuriae (>95%): arise from efferent arterioles of juxtamedullary Form hairpin medullary loops acting as Countercurrent Exchangers; preserve hypertonic medullary gradient without nephrons. Vasa Recta Verae: aglomerular, arise directly from

arcuate/interlobular arteries (aging/atrophy). washout. Sluggish flow (<10% RBF). Ludwig's Arteriole: branches from interlobular arteriole to peritubular plexus Capsular collaterals (from lumbar, suprarenal, & colic arteries)
maintain cortical viability and prevent total renal gangrene in bypassing glomerulus. Arteriae Perforantes: pierce capsule to anastomose

Unlike end-arteries, renal veins have rich anastomoses; ligation of Stellate veins (Verheyen) drain outer cortex -> Interlobular veins -> Arcuate Veins (form COMPLETE anastomosing arches) -> Interlobar veins -> Single an intrarenal vein branch is safe. Left renal vein compressed in

Renal Infarction: occlusion of segmental, arcuate, or interlobular end-arteries Papillary Necrosis: ischemic coagulative necrosis of pyramids due to compromised vasa recta in Diabetes, Sickle Cell, Analgesic
yields wedge-shaped pale infarcts (base at capsule, apex inward). abuse (NSAIDs), & Pyelonephritis.
